results.question: What drying temperature does Siemens give for Class F insulation, and what must be done before reaching it?
results.expected_answer: 245°F (118°C); Class F and H units are first baked at 70% of the specified temperature for about six hours
results.rewritten_query: Siemens Class F insulation drying temperature and required precautions before reaching the specified temperature.
results.answer:
## Siemens Class F drying temperature

| Insulation class | Drying temperature |
|---|---:|
| Class F | 245°F (118°C) [1] |

Before raising the winding to the drying temperature, bake it at **70% of the specified temperature for about six hours** to avoid steam forming inside the winding. [1] For Class F, this is approximately **172°F (83°C)**.

## Drying procedure and checks

1. Dry the windings when low insulation resistance is believed to be caused by excessive moisture. [1]
2. Use a warm-air oven, electric strip heaters, or circulating currents through the coils. [1]
3. Apply heat slowly so the desired temperature is not reached in less than six hours. [1]
4. Measure insulation resistance before applying heat and every six to eight hours thereafter. [1]
5. For electric strip-heater drying, remove the bearing housings and rotor, direct a fan at the stator, and attach temperature indicators to the winding. [2]
6. For warm-air-oven drying, remove the bearing housings and rotor, then bake at the specified temperature while following the insulation-drying procedure. [3]
7. Do not use radiant-type heaters, because some areas may scorch before remote areas reach the desired temperature. [2]

If the insulation resistance is less than satisfactory, and the cause is believed to be excessive moisture in the windings, dry the windings by applying heat from:

results.question: When shimming between flanges on a Siemens vertical motor, how thick should the minor shims be and how far may shims penetrate?
results.expected_answer: Minor shims are one-half the thickness of the major shim; shims must not penetrate deeper than the bolt hole circle and not be wider than twice the penetration distance (Figure 3)
results.rewritten_query: Siemens vertical motor flange shimming: recommended thickness for minor shims and maximum allowable shim penetration between flanges.
results.answer:
## Siemens shimming requirements

- **Minor shim thickness:** one-half the thickness of the major shim:  
  $$t_{\text{minor}}=\frac{1}{2}t_{\text{major}}$$
- **Maximum penetration:** shims must **not penetrate deeper than the bolt-hole circle**. Their width must be no more than twice the penetration distance:  
  $$w \leq 2p$$  
  where $p$ is the penetration distance. These limits help avoid twisting the flange. **[1]**

![Figure 3](diagrams/a03aca4e-dbdc-4868-a843-4c240457390e/fig3_1.png)

The context does not specify an absolute shim thickness or penetration distance; those depend on the flange geometry and the major shim thickness.

The purpose of a mounting flange for vertically mounted machines is to enable an easy installation and coupling connection, as well as an easy inspection of the coupling during operation. In order to fit the ABB machines, the mounting flanges shall be designed according to the IEC standard.

Round frame motors can be rotated within flange mounting bolt spacing to gain a satisfactory position for grease fittings and conduit attachments, and to mate run-out differences to avoid shimming flange fits. Terminal boxes without accessory devices can be turned to four equally spaced positions for access to conduit system; arrange the system so that water will not accumulate and drain into motor connection box.
1. Use a hoist; rig a sling around the lifting lugs.

7. Turn shaft again to check for free rotation.

contexts:
[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals
Rolling bearings of electrical machines need to be re-greased at regular intervals. The re-greasing interval is found on the bearing plate.
NOTE:
Regardless of the re-greasing interval, the bearings need to be re-greased at least once per year.
The re-greasing intervals are calculated for an operating temperature of 70°C (160°F). If the operating temperature is lower or higher than the assumed, the re-grease interval has to be altered accordingly. Higher operating temperature decreases the re-greasing interval.
NOTE:
An increase in the ambient temperature raises the temperature of the bearings correspondingly. The values for the re-greasing interval should be halved for every 15°C (30°F) increase in bearing temperature and may be once doubled for a 15°C (30°F) decrease in bearing temperature.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 66 · Figure 32 Example of lubrication channel through bearing arrangement of horizontal machine
NOTE:
NOTE:
Start-up greasing may take several grease portions (3-10 times amount mentioned at the lubrication plate).
The re-lubrication interval will never be longer than 12 months.
The type of original grease used is found on the bearing plate on the machine. Acceptable types of grease can be found in Chapter 7.5.3 Rolling bearings.
NOTE:
Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not mixture of two or more greases.
The temperature of the bearings will initially increase because of the excess grease. After few hours, the excess grease will be discharged through the lubrication valve and the temperature of the bearing will return to normal running temperature.
If available, and after the machine has been running for several hours, measure the vibrations or SPM-values from the SPM-nipples, and record the values for future reference use.
Following chapter for bearing type: Sleeve bearing

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 84 · 7.5.2.5 Oil change schedule for mineral oils
For self-lubricated bearings cleaning intervals with oil changes of approximately 8000 operating hours are recommended and approx. 20000 operating hours for bearings with oil circulation systems.
Shorter oil change intervals may be necessary in case of frequent start-ups, high oil temperatures or excessively high contamination due to external influences.
The correct oil change interval can be found on the bearing plate and dimensional drawing, see Chapter 2.1.2 Bearing plate.
Following chapter for bearing type: Rolling bearing

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · Manual re-greasing while the machine is running
Re-greasing while the machine is running:
- Verify that the grease to be used is suitable.
- Clean the grease nipples and the area around them.
- Verify that the lubrication channel is open, if equipped with a handle, open it.
- Press the specified amount and type of grease into the bearing.
- Let the machine run 1-2 hours in order to ensure that all excess grease is forced out of the bearing. The bearing temperature may temporarily increase during this time.
- If equipped with a handle, close it.
NOTE:
Beware of all rotating parts during the re-greasing.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.4 Re-greasing
All rolling bearings of rotating electrical machines need to be re-greased, see Chapter 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals. The re-greasing can be performed either manually or by means of an automatic system. In either case, it has to be verified that a suitable amount of the correct grease is entering the bearing at suitable intervals.
NOTE:
Grease can cause skin irritation and eye inflammation. Follow all safety precautions specified by the grease manufacturer.

results.question: What is the tightening torque for an M20 strength class 8.8 standard-thread screw on the Kohler KD27V12 engine?
results.rewritten_query: Kohler KD27V12 engine: tightening torque for an M20, property class 8.8, standard-thread screw.
results.answer:
## Tightening torque

For an **M20, strength class 8.8 screw with a standard thread**, use **390 Nm**. [1]

| Screw size | Thread type | Strength class | Tightening torque |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| M20 | Standard | 8.8 | **390 Nm** | [1]

## Verification and application

1. Verify that the screw is **M20**, **strength class 8.8**, and has a **standard thread**. [1]
2. Confirm that no separate tightening instruction applies for a fine-thread screw, since the listed standard values apply to standard threads. [1]
3. Check whether the screw has the specified **FLZN/480H surface treatment**; the corresponding table lists **335 Nm** for an M20 class 8.8 screw, so the applicable surface-treatment table must be confirmed before tightening. [1]
4. If the screw is not identified as FLZN/480H and no other instruction applies, tighten it to **390 Nm**. [1]

results.question: What is the tightening torque for an M12 strength class 10.9 screw on the Kohler KD27V12 engine?
results.rewritten_query: Kohler KD27V12 engine: tightening torque specification for an M12 strength class 10.9 screw.
results.answer:
## Tightening torque

For an **M12 strength-class 10.9 screw with a standard thread**, use **117 Nm**. [1]

| Screw size | Strength class 8.8 | Strength class 10.9 |
|---|---:|---:|
| M12 | 79 Nm | **117 Nm** [1] |

## Conditions and procedure

1. Confirm that the screw has a **standard thread**, because the Kohler manual states that fine-thread screws require a specific tightening instruction. [1]
2. Confirm that the screw is **strength class 10.9** and is being used as a standard screw fitting covered by the table. [1]
3. Set the torque wrench to **117 Nm** and tighten the screw according to the applicable assembly instructions. [1]
4. If the screw has the specified **FLZN/480H surface treatment**, the separate table lists **101 Nm** for an M12 strength-class 10.9 screw; the applicable table must therefore be confirmed before tightening. [1]

The provided context does not include a KD27V12-specific tightening sequence, lubrication condition, or torque-wrench tolerance.

results.question: If the fuel sulfur content is between 0.5% and 1%, how does the Kohler engine oil change interval change?
results.expected_answer: Oil change factor 1/2 — the interval is halved; limited to engine oil categories 2 and 3
results.rewritten_query: Kohler engine oil change interval for fuel sulfur content between 0.5% and 1%.
results.answer:
## Effect on the oil-change interval

For fuel sulfur content **greater than 0.5% and up to 1%**, the engine oil change interval is reduced by half, subject to use with **engine oil category 2 or 3**. [1]

| Fuel sulfur content | Applicable condition | Oil-change factor | Effect |
|---|---|---:|---|
| \(0.5\% < \text{sulfur} \le 1\%\) | Limited to engine oil category 2 and 3 | \(1/2\) | Reduces the maintenance interval by half. [1] |

The adjusted interval is calculated as:

$$
\text{Change interval}
=
\text{Basic change interval}
\times
\text{Oil-category factor}
\times
\frac{1}{2}
$$

[1]

## Procedure

1. Identify the basic interval from the applicable maintenance table for the genset application—ESP, PRP, or COP—and the engine injection calibration—EO or FO. [1]
2. Confirm that the engine oil is category 2 or 3, because this sulfur range is limited to those categories. [1]
3. Apply the sulfur-content factor of \(1/2\), thereby scheduling the oil change at half the otherwise applicable interval. [1]
4. Validate or adjust the interval through engine oil analysis if difficulty factors or severe operating conditions apply. [1][5]

Relevant difficulty factors include:

- Frequent cold starts. [1]
- Environmental influences. [1]
- Operating temperature. [1]
- Dust. [1]
- High humidity. [1]
- Long downtimes. [1]

results.answer:
## Conservation period

In normal storage in a **dry, ventilated place**, the Kohler engine’s conservation protection lasts **6 months from the date it is ready for delivery**. [1]

For longer or less favorable storage:

- If the engine is covered with a **waterproof film cover** that lies loosely against it and permits air circulation, outdoor storage is allowed for **up to 1 month**. [1]
- Longer outdoor storage, or storage in damp, unventilated conditions, is expected to **shorten the conservation-protection period**. [1]
- The provided Kohler information does **not specify a conservation period or detailed preservation procedure for storage beyond 6 months**.
- Storage conditions are the responsibility of the system manufacturer; ISO 6749-1984 should be observed for transport and storage, and only Kohler-approved preservatives should be used. [3]
- For uncertainties, contact Kohler customer service. [3]

## Approved coolant for KD27V12

For the KD27V12, use **only pre-mixed coolant of the same type**. The approved coolant technologies are **SI-OAT** or **hybrid technology with ethylene glycol**, at a recommended concentration of **40%–50%**. [1][3]

2. Maintain the coolant concentration at **40%–50%**. [1]
3. Monitor the coolant by analysis; the change interval may be adjusted if the analysis warrants it. [1]
4. Check that the coolant has a typical color, is clear, has a normal smell, and resembles new coolant. [1]
5. Check the coolant analysis limits:

| pH value | 6.7–9.0 [1] |
| Chloride | <100 mg/l [1] |

results.question: According to the Kohler KD27V12 manual, what permissible average power output over 24 hours applies to an ESP-rated and a PRP-rated generator?
results.source: 5.2.1 Nominal values of the power generator, p.49
results.expected_answer: ESP: not above 85% of the ESP rating (up to 200 h/year); PRP: not above 75% of the PRP rating
results.rewritten_query: According to the Kohler KD27V12 manual, what permissible average power output over a 24-hour period applies to ESP-rated versus PRP-rated generators?
results.answer:
## Permissible 24-hour average output

- **ESP-rated generator:** The permissible average power output over 24 hours is **no more than 85% of the ESP rating**. [1]
- **PRP-rated generator:** The permissible average power output over 24 hours is **no more than 75% of the PRP rating**. [2]

The limits can be expressed as:

$$
P_{\text{avg, ESP}} \leq 0.85 \times P_{\text{ESP}}
$$

$$
P_{\text{avg, PRP}} \leq 0.75 \times P_{\text{PRP}}
$$

The ESP definition applies to operation for up to 200 hours per year under specified conditions, while PRP applies to continuous operation for an unlimited number of hours per year under agreed operating conditions; in both cases, maintenance must follow the manufacturer’s instructions. [1][2]

results.question: What fuel pipe diameter does EMSA recommend for an 800–1500 kVA standby generator, and what are the pipe length and height limits?
results.expected_answer: 1 1/2 inch; maximum 6 m length, 0.9 m vertical height, 6 pipe fittings
results.rewritten_query: EMSA standby generator fuel system requirements for 800–1500 kVA models: recommended fuel pipe diameter, maximum pipe length, and maximum allowable height or vertical lift.
results.answer:
## Recommended fuel-pipe sizing

| Generator power, standby (kVA) | Recommended pipe diameter | Maximum pipe length | Maximum vertical height | Maximum pipe fittings |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 800–1500 | **1 1/2 in** | **6 m** | **0.9 m** | **6** [1] |

## Installation conditions and checks

- Positive static fuel pressure must be applied at the fuel-pump intake for fuel-tank applications installed with the standby generator assembly. [1]
- The maximum fuel level must not exceed **2 m above the crankshaft centre**; exceeding this level may cause engine damage. [1]
- The minimum fuel level must be **15 cm above the fuel-injection pump**; a lower level may prevent proper fuel pressure at the pump intake. [1]
- Check valves are required if the fuel tank is **2 m above the crankshaft centre**. [1]

## Basic installation sequence

1. Select a **1 1/2-inch** fuel pipe for the 800–1500 kVA standby generator range. [1]
2. Keep the total fuel-pipe length at or below **6 m**, the vertical height at or below **0.9 m**, and the number of fittings at or below **6**. [1]
3. Verify that the fuel system provides positive static pressure at the fuel-pump intake. [1]
4. Check the tank fuel level against the stated limits and install check valves where the tank is 2 m above the crankshaft centre. [1]

results.question: When adding electrolyte to an EMSA maintenance-type battery for the first time, what density and level are required, and how long is the minimum charge?
results.expected_answer: Specific density 1.280 at 20°C, filled to 15 mm above the plates (electrolyte above 10°C); minimum charging period 6 hours
results.rewritten_query: For the first electrolyte filling of an EMSA maintenance-type battery, what electrolyte density and electrolyte level are required, and what is the minimum charging time?
results.answer:
## Required values

- **Electrolyte density:** $1.270$–$1.280$ specific density, corresponding to a fully charged battery. The context does not explicitly state that this is the required *initial filling* density, only that it is the fully charged reference range. [3]
- **Electrolyte level:** Add distilled water until the level is **10 mm above the plates**. [1]
- **Minimum charging/check period:** Monitor the electrolyte level at **1-hour intervals**; the battery is considered charged when **no change is observed after 1 hour**. [1]

## Procedure

1. Fill the maintenance-type battery with electrolyte and verify its specific density with a hydrometer; the fully charged reference is $1.270$–$1.280$. [3]
2. Add distilled water until the electrolyte is 10 mm above the plates. [1]
3. Charge the battery and check the electrolyte level after 1 hour. [1]
4. Treat the battery as charged when no change in electrolyte level is observed after that 1-hour period. [1]

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 57 · 4.3.5 Insulation distances of main power connections
The connections of the main power cables must be designed to withstand demanding operation conditions where the insulators can be subjected to dirt, humidity and surge voltages. In order to ensure lasting and trouble-free running, it is therefore important that the length of the insulation and creepage distances are sufficient. The minimum insulation and creepage distances should be equal or exceed demands set by:
- Local requirements
- Standards
- Classification rules
- Hazardous area classification.
The insulation and creepage distances apply both for insulation distances between two different phases, and for insulation distances between one phase and earth. The air insulation distance is the shortest distance through air between two points with different electrical potential (voltage). The surface creepage distance is the shortest distance along surfaces next to each other between two points with different electrical potential (voltage).

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 57 · 4.3.6 Main power cables
The size of the input cables has to be adequate for the maximum load current and in accordance with local standards. The cable terminals have to be of appropriate type and of correct size. The connection to all devices has to be checked.
The main power cable connections should be tightened correctly to ensure reliable operation. For details, see Appendix Typical main power cable connections.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 60 · 4.3.10.3 Auxiliary cables
The auxiliary cables must be screened to meet the EMC requirements. Special cable glands must be used for the 360° high-frequency earthing of the cable screens at the cable entries.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 59 · 4.3.10.2 Earthing of main cable
The compliance with EMC directive requires high-frequency earthing of the main cable. This is achieved by a 360° earthing of the cable screens at the cable entries in both the machine and in the frequency converter. The earthing at the machine is implemented for example by means of the EMC ROX SYSTEM cable transits for shielded installations.
NOTE:
360° high-frequency earthing of cable entries is made in order to suppress electromagnetic disturbances. In addition, cable screens have to be connected to protective earth (PE) in order to meet safety regulations.

results.question: Which grease is the ABB example rolling-bearing plate (Figure 4) delivered with, and how often must the waste grease box be emptied?
results.expected_answer: ESSO UNIREX N2; empty the waste grease box every 6th relubrication
results.rewritten_query: For the ABB example rolling-bearing plate shown in Figure 4, which grease is supplied with the bearing, and how frequently must the waste-grease box be emptied?
results.answer:
## Direct answer

- The ABB example rolling-bearing plate is delivered from the factory with **ESSO UNIREX N2** grease. [1]  
  ![Figure 4 Bearing plate for grease lubricated rolling bearings](diagrams/41ec3469-76ef-43af-af26-ddc71f09336b/fig4_1.png)
- Empty the **waste grease box after every sixth relubrication**. [1]

## Relevant maintenance conditions

- The example plate specifies a relubrication interval of **8,800 duty hours at a 70°C (158°F) bearing temperature**. [1]
- The specified grease quantity is **80 g for the drive-end bearing and 80 g for the non-drive-end bearing**. [1]
- Every **15°C (59°F) increase above 70°C** bearing temperature halves the rated relubrication interval; above **85°C (185°F)**, high-temperature grease must be used. [1]
- If an automatic re-greasing system is used, the grease quantity indicated on the bearing plate must be **doubled**. [2]
- Greases must not be mixed; the bearing must contain only one type of grease. [3][4]

A variety of automatic re-lubrication systems is available on the market. However, ABB recommends only the use of electromechanical re-lubrication systems. [3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 66 · Figure 32 Example of lubrication channel through bearing arrangement of horizontal machine
NOTE:
NOTE:
Start-up greasing may take several grease portions (3-10 times amount mentioned at the lubrication plate).
The re-lubrication interval will never be longer than 12 months.
The type of original grease used is found on the bearing plate on the machine. Acceptable types of grease can be found in Chapter 7.5.3 Rolling bearings.
NOTE:
Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not mixture of two or more greases.
The temperature of the bearings will initially increase because of the excess grease. After few hours, the excess grease will be discharged through the lubrication valve and the temperature of the bearing will return to normal running temperature.
If available, and after the machine has been running for several hours, measure the vibrations or SPM-values from the SPM-nipples, and record the values for future reference use.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · 7.5.3.5 Bearing grease (table)
It is essential to use grease of good quality and with the correct base soap. This will ensure a long and trouble free lifetime of the bearings.
Grease used for re-greasing should have the following properties:
- Be special rolling bearing grease.
- Be of good quality with a lithium complex soap, and with mineral-, or PAO-oil.
- Have a base oil viscosity of 100 to 160 cSt at 40°C (105°F).
- Have a consistency NLGI grade between 1.5 and 3. For vertically or in hot conditions mounted machines, NLGI grade 2 or 3 is recommended.
- Have a continuous temperature range between -30°C (-20°F) and at least +120°C (250°F).
Grease with the correct properties is available from all major lubricant manufacturers. If the make of grease is changed and compatibility is uncertain, consult the manufacturing ABB factory, see Chapter 9.1.3 Contact information for Motors and Generators Service.
| NOTE: | Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not a mixture of two or more greases. |
| - | - |
| NOTE: | Grease additives are recommended. However, a written guarantee should be obtained from the lubricant manufacturer stating that the additives do not damage the bearings or the properties of the grease in the field of the operating temperature. This is especially important for EP additives. |
| NOTE: | Lubricants containing EP admixtures are not recommended. |

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 87 · Rolling bearing grease for extreme temperatures
If the bearing operating temperature is above 100°C (210°F), please consult the manufacturing ABB factory for suitable greases.

results.question: According to the Kohler KD27V12 manual's TBN chart (Fig. 27), below what TBN should the engine oil be exchanged as soon as possible?
results.rewritten_query: In the Kohler KD27V12 engine manual, according to the TBN chart in Figure 27, below what TBN value should the engine oil be changed as soon as possible?
results.answer:
## Limit

The engine oil should be exchanged as soon as possible when the TBN is **below 8 mg KOH/g**. [2]

![Fig. 27: The correlation between TBN and sulfur in fuel](diagrams/44763515-c04e-4c75-99ea-8eedffd37e93/fig27_1.png)

## Relevant conditions

- The TBN requirement is related to the sulfur content of the fuel, which influences combustion gases. [1]
- The chart’s TBN curves are for information only and are not binding. [3]
- The stated values do not apply to engine oils with low ash content. [3]
- For sulfur-containing fuel, only high-ash engine oils may be used, and the specified oil-change intervals must be observed. [3]

The provided context does not specify a TBN measurement procedure or further diagnostic steps beyond exchanging the oil as soon as possible when the value is below the stated limit.

The lubricating oil should be verified regarding the following aspects:
- Check the oil visually with respect to color, turbidity and deposits in a test bottle. The oil should be clear or negligibly turbid. The turbidity may not be caused by water.
- The water content must not exceed 0.2%.
- The original viscosity must be maintained within a tolerance of ±15%.
- The oil should be free from debris, and its cleanliness according to ISO 4406 class 18/15, or NAS 1638 class 9.
- The quantity of metal impurities should be less than 100 PPM. An increasing trend of the value means that the bearing is wearing.
- The total acid number (TAN) should not exceed 1 mg KOH per gram of oil. Please note that the TAN value is not the same as the TBN (total base number) value.
- Smell the oil. Strong acid or burnt smell is not acceptable.
An oil check should be performed a few days after the first test run of the machine, just before the first oil change, and subsequently as required. If the oil is changed just after the commissioning, it can be used again after removing wear particles by filtering or centrifuging.
In doubtful cases, an oil sample may be sent to the laboratory to determine viscosity, acid number, foaming tendency, etc.

results.question: Per NEMA MG1 as listed in the Siemens vertical motor manual, what is the unfiltered vibration limit for a resiliently mounted motor at 1800 RPM?
results.rewritten_query: According to NEMA MG 1 as cited in the Siemens vertical motor manual, what is the allowable unfiltered vibration limit for a resiliently mounted motor operating at 1800 RPM?
results.answer:
## Limit

For a resiliently mounted motor at **1800 RPM**, the NEMA MG1 unfiltered vibration limit is **0.15 in/s peak (3.8 mm/s peak)** at a rotational frequency of **30 Hz**. [1]

| Speed, RPM | Rotational frequency, Hz | Unfiltered velocity limit, in/s peak (mm/s) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1800 | 30 | 0.15 (3.8) [1] |

## Recommended check

1. Tighten the flange mounting bolts and check end play. [1]
2. Run the motor at minimum load and measure vibration. [1]
3. If vibration exceeds **0.15 in/s peak (3.8 mm/s peak)**, loosen the flange mounting bolts and shift the motor within the mounting-flange clearance. [1]
4. If shifting does not reduce vibration to the acceptable limit and the motor is coupled to a load, check shaft alignment and system reed frequency. [1]

[2] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 39 · Limits of Bearing Housing Vibration
Question: Please explain the limits of bearing housing vibration.
Answer: The following limits of vibration pertain to uncoupled, resiliently mounted machines, running at no load. For machines tested with rigid mounting, the values given should be multiplied by 0.8. Vibration levels given here refer to internally excited vibration only. Motors as installed (in situ) may exhibit higher levels.

results.question: For a Siemens vertical motor with a solid shaft, what total indicator readings are acceptable for parallel and angular alignment?

results.answer:
For a Siemens vertical motor with a solid shaft:

- **Parallel alignment:** total indicator readings must not exceed **0.002 in.** [1]

1. Check one plane at a time using a dial indicator mounted at the coupling. [1]

3. Slowly rotate both coupling halves through one complete turn. [1]
4. Record the indicator reading at each 90-degree increment from the starting point. [1]
5. Compare the total indicator readings with the applicable parallel or angular limit above. [1]

results.question: After regreasing a Siemens vertical motor's bearing, how long should the motor run before the drain plug is re-installed?
results.expected_answer: At least one (1) hour, to expel excess grease from the drain opening
results.rewritten_query: Siemens vertical motor bearing regreasing: required motor run time before reinstalling the grease drain plug.
results.answer:
## Required running time

The Siemens vertical motor should run for **at least one hour** after regreasing, with the drain plug removed, to expel excess grease before the drain plug is re-installed. [2]

## Procedure

1. Remove the drain plug—and the overflow plug, if fitted—and clean out hardened grease. [2]
2. Slowly pump the specified amount and type of compatible grease into the grease inlet. [2]
3. Replace the inlet plug and overflow plug, if fitted. [2]
4. Start the motor and run it for **at least one hour** so excess grease is expelled through the drain opening. [2]
5. Stop the motor and lock out the switch. [2]
6. Re-install the drain plug and return the motor to operation. [2]

[1] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 29 · Lubrication Instructions
Question: How can motors in service be relubricated?
Answer Units are pre-lubricated at the factory and do not require initial lubrication. Relubricating interval depends upon speed, type of bearing and service. Refer to table in the Operating and Instruction Manual provided with motor for suggested re-greasing intervals and recommended greases. Operating conditions may dictate more frequent lubrication. Motor must be at rest and electrical controls should be locked open to prevent energizing while motor is being serviced (refer to section on Safety). If motor is being taken out of storage, refer to storage procedures.
To re-lubricate bearings, remove the drain plug. Inspect grease drain and remove any blockage with a mechanical probe taking care not to damage bearing. Under no circumstances should a mechanical probe be used while the motor is in operation. Add new grease at the grease inlet. New grease must be compatible with grease already in the motor (refer to Table 1 in Operating & Maintenance Manual for replenishment quantities). Run the motor for 15 to 30 minutes with the drain plug removed to allow purging of any excess grease. Shut off unit and replace the drain plug. Return motor to service.

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 20 · Maintenance
For best results, grease should be compounded of a polyurea type and a good grade of petroleum oil and stabilized against oxidation.
The frequency of relubricating bearings and the amount added each time depends on two factors - speed and service.
All grease lube bearing motors will have affixed a plate with lubricating instructions. The instructions on this plate should be followed to achieve optimum bearing life and to avoid consequential damage to rotating parts.
Relubricate with the type of grease specified on the lubrication plate mounted on the motor, or compatible grease. Mixing of non-compatible greases can cause bearing failure.
Relubricate bearings with the proper grade of grease as follows:
1. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
2. Thoroughly clean the grease inlet fitting or plug. If the motor has a plug, remove plug and clean the inlet.
3. Remove the drain plug (and overflow plug, if so equipped) and clean out any hardened grease.
4. Slowly pump the correct amount of grease into the grease inlet, per the lubrication plate mounted on the motor. Replace inlet plug (and overflow plug, if so equipped).
5. Start motor and allow to run at least one (1) hour to expel any excess grease from the drain opening before re-installing the drain plug.
6. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
7. Re-install the drain plug.
8. Put the motor back in operation.

[3] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 20 · NOTE
If unit has been in operation for several years the old grease can harden. If this occurs remove bolts holding bottom inside end cap, raise end cap and wipe out hardened grease. Reassemble and add a small amount of fresh grease.
If machine is a totally-enclosed or weather-protected type disassembly of the lower bearing may be required to remove old grease. Also clean and refill inlet, overflow, and drain grease pipes.
Because the lower bearing is single shielded, the grease will not pass through the drain port unless the motor is run for some time.
Figure 4

Figures for this passage:
- Figure 4 — image path: diagrams/a03aca4e-dbdc-4868-a843-4c240457390e/fig4_1.png

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · Manual re-greasing while the machine is running
Re-greasing while the machine is running:
- Verify that the grease to be used is suitable.
- Clean the grease nipples and the area around them.
- Verify that the lubrication channel is open, if equipped with a handle, open it.
- Press the specified amount and type of grease into the bearing.
- Let the machine run 1-2 hours in order to ensure that all excess grease is forced out of the bearing. The bearing temperature may temporarily increase during this time.
- If equipped with a handle, close it.
NOTE:
Beware of all rotating parts during the re-greasing.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · Manual re-greasing while the machine is at a standstill
Preferably, re-grease the machine while it is running. If this is not possible, or considered dangerous, the re-greasing has to be carried out while the machine is at a standstill. In this case:
- Verify that the grease to be used is suitable.
- Stop the machine.
- Clean the grease nipples and the area around them.
- Verify that the lubrication channel is open, if equipped with a handle, open it.
- Press only half the amount of the specified type of grease into the bearing.
- Run the machine for a few minutes at full speed.
- Stop the machine.
- After the machine has stopped, press the specified amount of the correct grease into the bearing.
- Let the machine run 1-2 hours in order to ensure that all excess grease is forced out of the bearing. The bearing temperature may temporarily increase during this time.
- If equipped with a handle, close it.

results.question: What kind of grease does Siemens recommend for the bearings of its vertical induction motors?
results.expected_answer: A polyurea-type grease compounded with a good grade of petroleum oil and stabilized against oxidation (or the grease on the lubrication plate)
results.rewritten_query: Siemens-recommended grease for bearings in vertical induction motors.
results.answer:
## Recommended grease

Siemens recommends a grease **compounded of a polyurea type, made with good-grade petroleum oil, and stabilized against oxidation**. [3]

The motor’s lubrication plate remains the controlling reference for the specified grease type, relubrication interval, and quantity; Siemens permits the specified grease or a compatible grease. [3][4]

Mixing incompatible greases can cause bearing failure. [3]

## Relubrication procedure

1. Stop the motor and lock out the switch. [3]
2. Thoroughly clean the grease inlet fitting or plug; remove and clean the inlet plug if fitted. [3]
3. Remove the drain plug and overflow plug, if fitted, and clean out hardened grease. [3]
4. Slowly pump in the correct amount of the specified grease according to the motor’s lubrication plate, then replace the inlet and overflow plugs if fitted. [3]
5. Run the motor for at least one hour so excess grease can leave through the drain opening before reinstalling the drain plug. [3]
6. Stop the motor and lock out the switch. [3]
7. Reinstall the drain plug. [3]
8. Return the motor to operation. [3]

The Siemens material does not specify a universal NLGI grade, base-oil viscosity, temperature range, or grease brand; those details must be taken from the motor’s lubrication plate or obtained from Siemens where necessary.

results.question: When drying a Siemens vertical motor's stator by circulating direct current, how much current and DC voltage are usually needed?
results.expected_answer: Usually 50 to 100% of full load current; the DC voltage is 0.25–5.0% of normal voltage per phase (0.50–3.25% of the rating in power)
results.rewritten_query: Siemens vertical motor stator drying by circulating direct current: recommended drying current and DC voltage values.
results.answer:
## Required current and voltage

- **Current:** usually **50–100% of the motor’s full-load current**.  
- **DC voltage:** typically **0.25–5.0% of the normal voltage per phase**.  
- The corresponding power is typically **0.50–3.25% of the motor rating**. [2]

## Procedure and conditions

1. Use an external low-voltage DC source, such as a portable motor-generator welding set, to circulate current through the stator winding. [1]

2. Remove the bearing housings. [1]

3. Center the rotor in the stator core. [1]

4. Wedge fiber strips into the lower air gap to prevent rotor-to-stator contact, or remove the rotor. [1]

5. Arrange the stator phases in series or parallel if both ends of all phases are accessible. [2]

6. If only three motor leads are available, connect the current between one terminal and the other two terminals connected together. [2]

7. Check the temperature of the single-lead connection frequently in the three-lead arrangement, and shift the leads occasionally. [2]

8. Direct a fan onto the motor to remove excess moisture. [1]

9. Attach temperature indicators to the windings and do not exceed the specified insulation-drying temperatures. [1]

10. Avoid hot spots and radiant-type heat, which may damage the insulation. [2]

The specific maximum drying-temperature values cannot be stated because the referenced Insulation Drying Temperature table is not included in the provided context.

1. Remove bearing housings.

[4] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 16 · Maintenance Checklist
1. Verify motor is clean and verify that stator and rotor ventilation passages are unobstructed.
2. Check for excessive loading or service factor.
3. Verify winding temperature rise not in excess of rated value.
4. Verify insulation resistance is above recommended minimum.
5. Verify voltage and frequency variation.
6. Check air gap.
7. Verify that bearing temperatures are within limits and that lubricant is clean and proper level maintained.
8. Verify no unusual vibration or noise exists.
9. Check alignment.
10. Check for proper lubrication.
A definite schedule of preventive maintenance inspections should be established to avoid breakdown, serious damage and extensive downtime. The schedule will depend on operating conditions and experience with similar equipment. Question: After storing my motor for an extended period of time, I am now ready to install it. Is there any specific inspection procedure that must be followed?
Answer: Yes. Following storage, an extensive inspection must be performed on a motor by one of our authorized service stations. This inspection must include the following elements:
- 1) Render an external inspection of the motor to assure the unit is clean, ventilation openings are free of obstructions, and no damage has occurred.
- 2) Perform a megger test of motor windings to insure satisfactory insulation resistance.
- 3) Rotate the shaft to check for roughness in bearings or interference between rotating and stationary parts.
- 4) Perform a bench test on the unit to check for excessive amp. draw, noise, or vibration.
- 5) Regrease the motor bearings (as applicable) in accordance with the unit's operating instruction folder.
- 6) The authorized service station must install a plate/tag indicating the date of inspection. Make any corrections which inspection shows to be needed.

Motors are shipped in first class condition. They have been inspected and are skidded to prevent damage from ordinary handling during shipment.
Inspect new motors for shipping invoice. Make the examination before removing from cars or trucks. If damage or indication of rough handling is evident, file a claim with the carrier at once, and notify your Siemens sales representative.
Remove only the shipping invoice. Do not remove tags pertaining to lubrication, operation and storage instructions. Read and follow all instructions to insure that no damage to motor bearings, (due to condensation) and motor windings occurs during storage.

results.question: How should MICLAD VPI stator coils on a Siemens vertical motor be cleaned and baked?
results.expected_answer: With a quick-drying solvent and lint-free cloths, or low-pressure steam; then oven-bake the whole stator at 200°F for 12 hours and then 230°F for 12 hours
results.rewritten_query: Cleaning and baking procedure for MICLAD VPI stator coils in a Siemens vertical motor.
results.answer:
## Cleaning and baking procedure

MICLAD™ VPI stator coils may be cleaned with a quick-drying solvent and lint-free cloths, or with low-pressure steam; the entire stator must then be oven-baked at **200°F for 12 hours**, followed by **230°F for 12 hours**. [1]

1. Measure the stator-winding insulation resistance before cleaning. [1]
2. Select one cleaning method:
   - Wipe the coils with a quick-drying solvent and lint-free cloths. [1]
   - Steam-clean them using low-pressure steam. [1]
   - Alternatively, use water and detergent with an oven-drying cycle, provided the insulation system is MICLAD™ VPI. [1]
3. If using solvent, ensure it is compatible with the insulation system. [1]
4. Oven-bake the entire stator at **200°F for 12 hours**. [1]
5. Continue oven baking at **230°F for 12 hours**. [1]
6. Measure the stator-winding insulation resistance again after cleaning and drying. [1]

Cleaning frequency should be based on the actual operating conditions around the motor, and ventilation passages should be kept free of dirt, dust, and other debris. [5]

results.question: How should the re-greasing interval of an ABB machine's rolling bearings change with bearing temperature, and what is the minimum re-greasing frequency?
results.expected_answer: Intervals assume 70°C (160°F); halve them for every 15°C (30°F) increase, and they may be doubled once for a 15°C decrease; re-grease at least once per year regardless
results.rewritten_query: How should the rolling-bearing re-greasing interval for an ABB machine be adjusted based on bearing temperature, and what is the minimum allowable re-greasing frequency?
results.answer:
## Re-greasing interval

- Use the interval specified on the machine’s bearing plate as the baseline for a bearing operating at **70°C (160°F)**. [1]
- For every **15°C (30°F) increase** in bearing temperature, **halve** the re-greasing interval. [1]
- For every **15°C (30°F) decrease**, the interval **may be doubled**. [1]
- Regardless of the calculated interval, re-grease the bearings **at least once per year**; the interval must never exceed **12 months**. [1][5]

## Maintenance procedure

1. Check the bearing plate for the specified re-greasing interval and grease type. [1][5]
2. Determine the actual bearing operating temperature and adjust the bearing-plate interval using the 15°C temperature rules above. [1]
3. Apply the resulting interval, but cap it at **12 months** even if the temperature adjustment would produce a longer period. [1][5]
4. If the bearing operating temperature exceeds **100°C (210°F)**, consult the ABB manufacturing factory for a suitable grease. [4]
5. Do not mix greases; only one grease type should be present inside the bearing. [5]

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals
Rolling bearings of electrical machines need to be re-greased at regular intervals. The re-greasing interval is found on the bearing plate.
NOTE:
Regardless of the re-greasing interval, the bearings need to be re-greased at least once per year.
The re-greasing intervals are calculated for an operating temperature of 70°C (160°F). If the operating temperature is lower or higher than the assumed, the re-grease interval has to be altered accordingly. Higher operating temperature decreases the re-greasing interval.
NOTE:
An increase in the ambient temperature raises the temperature of the bearings correspondingly. The values for the re-greasing interval should be halved for every 15°C (30°F) increase in bearing temperature and may be once doubled for a 15°C (30°F) decrease in bearing temperature.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · Automatic re-greasing
A variety of automatic re-lubrication systems is available on the market. However, ABB recommends only the use of electromechanical re-lubrication systems. The quality of the grease entering the bearing has to be checked at least once per year: the grease has to look and feel like new grease. Any separation of the base oil from the soap is not acceptable.
NOTE:
If an automatic re-greasing system is used, double the amount of grease indicated on the bearing plate.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.4 Re-greasing
All rolling bearings of rotating electrical machines need to be re-greased, see Chapter 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals. The re-greasing can be performed either manually or by means of an automatic system. In either case, it has to be verified that a suitable amount of the correct grease is entering the bearing at suitable intervals.
NOTE:
Grease can cause skin irritation and eye inflammation. Follow all safety precautions specified by the grease manufacturer.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 87 · Rolling bearing grease for extreme temperatures
If the bearing operating temperature is above 100°C (210°F), please consult the manufacturing ABB factory for suitable greases.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 66 · Figure 32 Example of lubrication channel through bearing arrangement of horizontal machine
NOTE:
NOTE:
Start-up greasing may take several grease portions (3-10 times amount mentioned at the lubrication plate).
The re-lubrication interval will never be longer than 12 months.
The type of original grease used is found on the bearing plate on the machine. Acceptable types of grease can be found in Chapter 7.5.3 Rolling bearings.
NOTE:
Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not mixture of two or more greases.
The temperature of the bearings will initially increase because of the excess grease. After few hours, the excess grease will be discharged through the lubrication valve and the temperature of the bearing will return to normal running temperature.
If available, and after the machine has been running for several hours, measure the vibrations or SPM-values from the SPM-nipples, and record the values for future reference use.

Re-greasing while the machine is running:
- Verify that the grease to be used is suitable.
- Clean the grease nipples and the area around them.
- Verify that the lubrication channel is open, if equipped with a handle, open it.
- Press the specified amount and type of grease into the bearing.
- Let the machine run 1-2 hours in order to ensure that all excess grease is forced out of the bearing. The bearing temperature may temporarily increase during this time.

Preferably, re-grease the machine while it is running. If this is not possible, or considered dangerous, the re-greasing has to be carried out while the machine is at a standstill. In this case:
- Verify that the grease to be used is suitable.
- Stop the machine.
- Clean the grease nipples and the area around them.
- Verify that the lubrication channel is open, if equipped with a handle, open it.
- Press only half the amount of the specified type of grease into the bearing.
- Run the machine for a few minutes at full speed.
- Stop the machine.
- After the machine has stopped, press the specified amount of the correct grease into the bearing.
- Let the machine run 1-2 hours in order to ensure that all excess grease is forced out of the bearing. The bearing temperature may temporarily increase during this time.
- If equipped with a handle, close it.

During bearing maintenance, ensure that:
- No dirt or foreign debris is allowed to enter the bearings at any time during the maintenance.
- The bearings are washed, dried and pre-greased with suitable and high quality rolling bearing grease before assembly.
- The disassembly and mounting of the bearings does not damage the bearings. The bearings must be removed by using pullers and fitted by heating, or using special tools for the purpose.
If there is a need to change bearings, please contact ABB Motors and Generators Service. See Motors and Generators contact information in Chapter 9.1.3 Contact information for Motors and Generators Service.

results.question: What is the tightening torque for an M16 strength class 8.8 standard-thread screw on the Kohler KD27V12 engine?
results.rewritten_query: Kohler KD27V12 engine: tightening torque for a standard-thread M16, property class 8.8 screw.
results.answer:
## Tightening torque

For an **M16, strength class 8.8, metric standard-thread screw**, use **195 Nm** under the standard Kohler torque table. [1]

| Screw size | Strength class | Tightening torque |
|---|---:|---:|
| M16 | 8.8 | **195 Nm** [1] |

## Conditions and possible variation

- The value applies to **standard threads**; screws with fine threads require a specific tightening instruction. [1]
- If the screw has the listed **FLZN/480H matte-gray surface treatment**, the corresponding M16, class 8.8 value is **166 Nm** rather than 195 Nm. [1]
- The provided context does not identify whether the KD27V12 screw has that surface treatment or whether a separate engine-specific instruction overrides the general table, so the applicable value cannot be confirmed beyond these table conditions.

## Procedure

1. Confirm that the screw is **M16**, strength class **8.8**, and has a standard rather than fine thread. [1]
2. Check whether the screw has the **FLZN/480H matte-gray surface treatment**. [1]
3. Set the torque tool to **195 Nm** for the general standard-thread entry, or **166 Nm** if the FLZN/480H-specific entry applies. [1]
4. Tighten the screw to the selected value.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 114 · 8.3.2 Pt-100 resistance temperature detectors
Pt-100 resistance temperature detectors are an essential part in the machine's condition monitoring and protection system. They are used to measure temperatures in the windings, bearings and in the cooling air. The Pt-100 detector uses a fine platinum filament for the temperature measurement, which can be damaged e.g. by incorrect handling or excessive vibration.
The following symptoms might suggest a problem in a Pt-100 detector:
- Infinite or zero resistance over the detector
- Disappearance of measurement signal during, or after start up
- A significantly different resistance value in a single detector.
If a Pt-100 failure is suspected the findings should always be confirmed from the connection box, by measuring the resistance at the detector with its cables disconnected. The findings should by registered. For the correct measuring current see the appropriate Pt-100 detector. For resistance values at different temperatures, see Table 11 Temperature values for Pt-100 elements.

results.question: How many newton-metres should an oiled M20 grade 8.8 bolt be torqued to on an ABB machine?
results.rewritten_query: Torque specification in newton-metres for an oiled M20, grade 8.8 bolt on an ABB electric machine.
results.answer:
## Required torque

An **oiled M20 grade 8.8 bolt on an ABB machine should be torqued to 360 N·m**. [1]

| Bolt size | Property class | Condition | Torque |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| M20 | 8.8 | Oiled | **360 N·m** (270 lbf·ft) [1] |

## Conditions and checks

1. Verify that the fastening is a standard fastening covered by ABB’s general torque table. [1]
2. Do not apply this value to diodes, support insulators, bearings, cable terminals or pole fastenings, bus-bar terminals, surge arrestors, capacitors, current transformers, rectifier or thyristor bridges, or any item for which another torque is specified elsewhere in the manual. [1]
3. Regularly verify the tightness of all fastenings, with particular attention to grouting, anchor bolts, and rotor parts. [1]
4. Treat loose fastenings in these areas as a serious condition because they can cause sudden and severe damage to the machine. [1]

results.question: On a rigidly mounted ABB machine, which RMS vibration velocity separates zone B from zone C?
results.rewritten_query: ABB rigidly mounted machine RMS vibration velocity limit separating vibration severity zones B and C.
results.answer:
## Direct answer

On a **rigidly mounted ABB machine**, the RMS vibration velocity separating **Zone B from Zone C is 4.5 mm/s RMS**. [1]

| Support class | Zone boundary | RMS velocity |
|---|---:|---:|
| Rigid | B/C | 4.5 mm/s RMS [1] |

This classification applies to large machines rated above 300 kW and up to 50 MW, and to electrical machines with shaft height of at least 315 mm. [1]

## Related limits and procedure

For comparison, ABB lists an initial **ALARM** value of 3.4 mm/s RMS and a **TRIP** value of 7.1 mm/s RMS for rigidly supported machines. [2]

1. Measure broad-band RMS vibration with equipment having a flat response from at least 10 Hz to 1,000 Hz, in accordance with ISO 2954 requirements. [5]
2. Compare the measured value with the rigid-support boundary of 4.5 mm/s RMS. [1]
3. Treat vibration in Zone C as normally unsatisfactory for long-term continuous operation; the machine may generally be operated only for a limited period until remedial action is available. [1]
4. Establish the machine’s steady-state on-site baseline after a period of operation and adjust the alarm setting accordingly. [2]

The provided context does not identify specific root causes of vibration or prescribe remedial actions for a value above 4.5 mm/s RMS.

results.question: whats the lowest insulation resistance thats ok for a used stator winding on an ABB motor
results.rewritten_query: Minimum acceptable insulation resistance for a used ABB motor stator winding.
results.answer:
## Minimum acceptable value

For an **ABB motor’s used stator winding**, the insulation resistance should be **greater than 100 MΩ**, measured at **40 °C** after the test voltage has been applied for **1 minute or longer**. [2]

## Test conditions and procedure

1. Use an insulation resistance meter at **1000 VDC** and record the value after **1 minute**. [4]

2. Disconnect all power-supply cables and ensure the motor frame and stator windings not under test are earthed. [4]

3. Earth all resistance temperature detectors and verify that current-transformer secondary connections, including spare cores, are not open. [4]

4. Measure at the terminal box, normally between the motor frame and the complete stator winding with the three phases connected at the neutral point. [4]

5. Earth the winding phases briefly after the test to discharge them and reduce shock risk. [4]

If the resistance is below the specified value, investigate the cause; excess humidity or dirt commonly lowers the reading even when the insulation itself remains intact. [2]

[1] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 18 · Insulation Resistance
Check insulation resistance periodically. Use a hand cranked or solid state insulation resistance tester and test with at least 500 volts, but not greater than motor rated voltage.
For motors with newer insulation systems such as MICLAD™ VPI, the insulation resistance after one minute should be greater than 1000 megohms. (Values in excess of 5000 megohms are common.) For older motors, the minimum value recommended in IEEE Standard 43 can be used. The value in megohms, when corrected to 40°C, is equal to the motor rated voltage in kilovolts plus 1. For example, for a motor with a rated voltage of 2300 volts, the limit value would be:
2.3 + 1 = 3.3 (megohms).

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 92 · 7.6.4.3 Minimum values for insulation resistance
Criteria for windings in a normal condition:
Generally, the insulation resistance values for dry windings should exceed the minimum values significantly. Definite values are impossible to give, because resistance varies depending on the machine type and local conditions. In addition, the insulation resistance is affected by the age and usage of the machine. Therefore, the following values can only be considered as guidelines.
The insulation resistance limits, which are given below, are valid at 40 °C, and when the test voltage has been applied for 1 minute or longer.
- Rotor.
For induction machines with wound rotors: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 5 MΩ.
NOTE:
- Stator.
For new stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 1000 MΩ. If the measuring conditions are extremely warm and humid, R(1-10 min at 40 °C) values above 100 MΩ can be accepted.
For used stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 100 MΩ.
NOTE:
If the values given here are not reached, the reason for the low insulation resistance should be determined. A low insulation resistance value is often caused by excess humidity or dirt, although the actual insulation is intact.

[3] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 10 · Insulation Resistance
Check insulation resistance prior to connecting motor to power supply. A hand cranked or solid state electronic insulation resistance tester, at least 500 volts d.c., but not over rated voltage, is usually used (see Maintenance).
See IEEE Recommended Practice for Testing Insulation Resistance Rotating Machinery IEEE Std 43.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 92 · 7.6.4.4 Stator winding insulation resistance measurement
The insulation resistance is measured using an insulation resistance meter. The test voltage is 1000 VDC. The test time is 1 minute, after which the insulation resistance value is recorded. Before the insulation resistance test is conducted, the following actions must be taken:
- Check that the secondary connections of the current transformers (CT's), including spare cores are not open. See Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
- Verify that all power supply cables are disconnected.
- Verify that the frame of the machine and the stator windings not being tested are earthed.
- The winding temperature is measured.
- All resistance temperature detectors are earthed.
- Possible earthing of voltage transformers (not common) must be removed.
The insulation resistance measuring should be carried out in the terminal box. The test is usually performed to the whole winding as a group, in which case the meter is connected between the frame of the machine and the winding; See Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements. The frame is earthed and the three phases of the stator winding remain connected at the neutral point, see Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
If the measured insulation resistance of the whole winding is lower than specified, and the phase windings can easily be disconnected from each other, each phase can also be measured separately. This is not possible for all machines. In this measurement, the tester is connected between the frame of the machine and one of the windings. The frame and the two phases not measured are earthed; see Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
Carbon dust on slip rings and naked copper surfaces lower the insulation resistance values of the rotor.
When phases are measured separately, all star-points of the winding system must be removed. If the star-point of the component cannot be removed, as in a typical tri-phase voltage transformer, the whole component must be removed.
Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements
- a) Insulation resistance measurement for star connected winding.
- b) Insulation resistance measurement for delta connected winding.
- c) Insulation resistance measurement for one phase of the winding. The 'MΩ' represents the insulation resistance meter.
After the insulation resistance measurement the winding phases must be earthed briefly in order to discharge them.
Following chapter for rotor type: Slip rings

Figures for this passage:
- Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements — image path: diagrams/41ec3469-76ef-43af-af26-ddc71f09336b/fig39_1.png

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 90 · 7.6.4 Insulation resistance test
During general maintenance work and before the machine is started up for the first time or after a long period of standstill, the insulation resistance of stator and rotor windings must be measured.
The insulation resistance measurement provides information about the humidity and dirtiness of the insulation. Based upon this information, correct cleaning and drying actions can be determined.
For new machines with dry windings, the insulation resistance is very high. The resistance can, however, be extremely low if the machine has been subjected to incorrect transportation and storage conditions and humidity, or if the machine is operated incorrectly.
NOTE:
Windings should be earthed briefly immediately after measurement in order to avoid risk of electric shock.

results.question: Roughly how many direct-on-line starts per year is an ABB induction machine designed for?
results.rewritten_query: How many direct-on-line (DOL) starts per year is an ABB induction machine designed to withstand?
results.answer:
## Direct answer

As a general guideline, an ABB direct-on-line induction machine may be started **about 1,000 times per year** in a typical application. This is not a universal design limit. [1]

The actual allowable number depends on:

- Load torque versus rotational speed and load inertia. [1]
- The machine type and design. [1]
- The manufacturer’s performance data sheet. [1]

Excessive or heavy starting can cause abnormally high temperatures and mechanical stresses, accelerating ageing, shortening service life, or causing machine failure. [1]

## Recommended procedure

1. Check the machine’s performance data sheet for the permitted consecutive and annual starts. [1]
2. Consult the manufacturer if the permitted starting frequency is not stated. [1]
3. Evaluate the application load characteristics, including the torque curve and inertia. [1]
4. Use a counter system to control the number of starts. [1]
5. Set maintenance intervals based on equivalent operating hours. [1]

The number of allowed consecutive starts of direct on line supplied machines depends essentially on the load characteristics (torque curve vs. rotational speed, inertia), and on the machine type and design. The provided context does not include the formula required to calculate equivalent operating hours for a fixed-speed drive, so the calculation cannot be completed from the available information.

ABB states that equivalent operating hours are calculated using a formula, but that formula is not present in the supplied extract. [1]

The context only establishes that:

- ABB’s maintenance program uses four maintenance levels that rotate according to operating hours. [1]
- Level 1 consists mainly of quick visual inspections, while Level 4 involves more demanding measurements and replacements. [1]
- The recommended maintenance program is a minimum level and should be intensified for demanding local conditions or very high reliability requirements. [1]
- Normal supervision and observation of the machine’s condition are required even when the program is followed. [1]

For a fixed-speed-drive calculation, the missing information is the ABB equivalent-hours formula and any fixed-speed operating factors or conditions used by that formula.

This chapter presents a recommended maintenance program for ABB machines. This maintenance program is of a general nature, and should be considered as a minimum level of maintenance. Maintenance should be intensified when local conditions are demanding or very high reliability is required. It should also be noted that even when following this maintenance program, normal supervision and observation of the machine's condition is required.

The maintenance program is based on four levels of maintenance, which rotate according to operating hours. The amount of work and down time vary, so that level 1 includes mainly quick visual inspections and level 4 more demanding measurements and replacements. More information about the spare part packages suitable for these maintenances can be found in Chapter 9.2 Spare parts for rotating electrical machines. results.question: For ABB flood-lubricated sleeve bearings, what oil feed pressure is considered normal?
results.rewritten_query: Normal oil feed pressure for ABB flood-lubricated sleeve bearings.
results.answer:
## Normal oil feed pressure

For ABB flood-lubricated sleeve bearings, the normal oil supply pressure is **125 kPa ± 25 kPa**, equivalent to **18 psi ± 4 psi**. [5]

This pressure provides the correct oil flow to the bearing; a higher supply pressure provides no additional benefit and may cause oil leakage. [5]

1. Adjust the supply pressure using the pressure valve and orifice. [5]
2. Verify the required oil flow against the rate specified on the machine’s dimensional drawing. [5]
3. Confirm the machine-specific pressure from the documentation supplied with the machine. [4]

The oil level of a self-lubricated sleeve bearing needs to be checked regularly. The correct oil level is in the middle of the oil sight glass, but as long as the oil level is within the oil sight glass, the level is acceptable.

Verify that no rotating parts rub against any stationary parts. Verify through the oil sight glass that the oil level inside bearing is correct. The correct oil level is in the middle of the oil sight glass, but as long as the oil level is within the oil sight glass, the level is acceptable.
Check the temperature and the oil level of the bearings continuously in the beginning. This is particularly important for self-lubricating bearings. If the temperature of the bearing suddenly rises, the machine should be stopped immediately, and the reason for the temperature rise must be found before the machine is re-started. If no logical reason is found from the measurement equipment, it is recommended that the bearing is opened, and its condition verified. If the machine is under warranty, the manufacturing factory must always be contacted before any action is taken.
For self-lubricating bearings, the rotation of the oil ring is verified through the inspection window on top of the bearing. If the oil ring is not rotating, the machine must be stopped immediately, as a stopped oil ring will result in bearing failure.

This gives the right flow of oil to the bearing. Using higher supply pressure gives no additional benefit, but can cause bearing oil leakages. The rate of oil flow is also specified on the dimensional drawing.

results.question: ABB class F stator - minimum PI?
results.rewritten_query: ABB Class F motor stator insulation — minimum polarization index (PI) value for insulation resistance testing
results.answer:
## Minimum PI

The minimum polarization index (PI) for an ABB class F stator winding is **greater than 2**. [1]

- PI is determined by measuring insulation resistance after **1 minute and 10 minutes**; the passage also permits a **15-second and 1-minute** measurement. [1]
- PI values typically range from **1 to 4**; values close to 1 indicate humid or dirty windings. [1]
- The test should be performed with the winding temperature **at or below 50 °C (122 °F)**, because higher temperatures can cause unpredictable PI changes. [1]
- Dirt and humidity can reduce both insulation resistance and PI. [1]

For the related insulation-resistance check, ABB specifies that the test voltage is **1000 VDC** and the test duration is **1 minute**. [5]

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 94 · 7.6.6 The polarization index
For the polarization index test the insulation resistance is measured after the voltage has been applied for 15 seconds and 1 minute (or 1 minute and 10 minutes). The polarization index test is less dependent on the temperature than the insulation resistance. When the winding temperature is below 50ºC (122ºF), it may be considered independent of temperature. High temperatures can cause unpredictable changes in the polarization index, therefore the test should not be used at temperatures above 50ºC (122ºF).
Dirt and humidity accumulating in the winding normally reduces the insulation resistance, and the polarization index, as well as their dependence on temperature. Thus, the line in Figure 38 Correlation between the insulation resistance and the temperature becomes less steep. Windings with open creepage distances are very sensitive to the effects of dirt and humidity.
There are several rules for determining the lowest acceptable value with which the machine can be safely started. For the polarization index (PI), the values usually range between 1 and 4. Values close to 1 indicate that the windings are humid and dirty.
The minimum PI value for class F stator windings is more than 2.

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 18 · Insulation Resistance
Check insulation resistance periodically. Use a hand cranked or solid state insulation resistance tester and test with at least 500 volts, but not greater than motor rated voltage.
For motors with newer insulation systems such as MICLAD™ VPI, the insulation resistance after one minute should be greater than 1000 megohms. (Values in excess of 5000 megohms are common.) For older motors, the minimum value recommended in IEEE Standard 43 can be used. The value in megohms, when corrected to 40°C, is equal to the motor rated voltage in kilovolts plus 1. For example, for a motor with a rated voltage of 2300 volts, the limit value would be:
2.3 + 1 = 3.3 (megohms).

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 92 · 7.6.4.3 Minimum values for insulation resistance
Criteria for windings in a normal condition:
Generally, the insulation resistance values for dry windings should exceed the minimum values significantly. Definite values are impossible to give, because resistance varies depending on the machine type and local conditions. In addition, the insulation resistance is affected by the age and usage of the machine. Therefore, the following values can only be considered as guidelines.
The insulation resistance limits, which are given below, are valid at 40 °C, and when the test voltage has been applied for 1 minute or longer.
- Rotor.
For induction machines with wound rotors: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 5 MΩ.
NOTE:
- Stator.
For new stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 1000 MΩ. If the measuring conditions are extremely warm and humid, R(1-10 min at 40 °C) values above 100 MΩ can be accepted.
For used stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 100 MΩ.
NOTE:
If the values given here are not reached, the reason for the low insulation resistance should be determined. A low insulation resistance value is often caused by excess humidity or dirt, although the actual insulation is intact.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 94 · 7.6.5 Insulation resistance measurement for auxiliaries
To ensure correct operation of the machines protections and other auxiliaries, their condition can be determined by an insulation resistance test. The procedure is described in detail in Chapter 7.6 Maintenance of stator and rotor windings. The test voltage for the space heater should be 500 VDC and for other auxiliaries 100 VDC. The insulation resistance measurement for Pt-100 detectors or proximity probes is not recommended.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 92 · 7.6.4.4 Stator winding insulation resistance measurement
The insulation resistance is measured using an insulation resistance meter. The test voltage is 1000 VDC. The test time is 1 minute, after which the insulation resistance value is recorded. Before the insulation resistance test is conducted, the following actions must be taken:
- Check that the secondary connections of the current transformers (CT's), including spare cores are not open. See Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
- Verify that all power supply cables are disconnected.
- Verify that the frame of the machine and the stator windings not being tested are earthed.
- The winding temperature is measured.
- All resistance temperature detectors are earthed.
- Possible earthing of voltage transformers (not common) must be removed.
The insulation resistance measuring should be carried out in the terminal box. The test is usually performed to the whole winding as a group, in which case the meter is connected between the frame of the machine and the winding; See Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements. The frame is earthed and the three phases of the stator winding remain connected at the neutral point, see Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
If the measured insulation resistance of the whole winding is lower than specified, and the phase windings can easily be disconnected from each other, each phase can also be measured separately. This is not possible for all machines. In this measurement, the tester is connected between the frame of the machine and one of the windings. The frame and the two phases not measured are earthed; see Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements.
Carbon dust on slip rings and naked copper surfaces lower the insulation resistance values of the rotor.
When phases are measured separately, all star-points of the winding system must be removed. If the star-point of the component cannot be removed, as in a typical tri-phase voltage transformer, the whole component must be removed.
Figure 39 Connections of the stator windings for insulation resistance measurements
- a) Insulation resistance measurement for star connected winding.
- b) Insulation resistance measurement for delta connected winding.
- c) Insulation resistance measurement for one phase of the winding. The 'MΩ' represents the insulation resistance meter.
After the insulation resistance measurement the winding phases must be earthed briefly in order to discharge them.

results.question: What contact pressure should the slip-ring brushes on an ABB machine press with?
results.rewritten_query: Recommended contact pressure for carbon brushes on ABB machine slip rings.
results.answer:
## Required contact pressure

The slip-ring brushes should press with **18–20 mN/mm²**, equivalent to **180–200 g/cm²**, evenly distributed over the entire contact surface so the brush conforms to the slip-ring curvature. **[2]**

## Measurement procedure

1. Attach a spring balance to the tip of the lever pressing the brush. **[2]**
2. Pull the spring balance radially until the pressure is just relieved from the brush. **[2]**
3. Use a piece of paper between the brush and the press lever to detect when the pressure is relieved. **[2]**

![Figure 41 Checking brush pressure with spring balance](diagrams/41ec3469-76ef-43af-af26-ddc71f09336b/fig41_1.png)

## If wear is rapid or uneven

Check the following:

- Whether the brush pressure is within the specified **18–20 mN/mm²** range. **[2][5]**
- Whether all brush pigtail cables are reliably connected. **[5]**
- Whether the slip-ring sliding surfaces have deteriorated; the surfaces should be smooth and clean. **[3][5]**
- Whether the carbon brushes may have absorbed oil or moisture. **[5]**
- Whether the brush quality is specified for the machine. **[5]**
- Whether the brushes are in good condition and move freely in their holders. **[5]**
- Remove coal dust by vacuum cleaning. **[5]**

The slip ring unit of the permanent contact type is equipped with filter for carbon dust. The cleaning interval of the filter in respect to carbon brush wear is shown in Figure 42 Maximum cleaning interval of the slip ring housing carbon dust filter, parameter brush wear in mm/10³ h.
The slip ring housing is equipped with a differential pressure switch for monitoring the condition of the filters. The filter must be changed immediately after an alarm. It is also highly recommended that the operating personnel manually inspects the filters frequently.
The carbon dust filter can be cleaned by washing, beating, or spraying.
Figure 42 Maximum cleaning interval of the slip ring housing carbon dust filter, parameter brush wear in mm/10³ h
